subject: Annual commit tiers & hosted API pricing — playbook for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@nimbushealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exploring annual commit options for hosted API

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — Nimbus is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. We are evaluating an annual commit to stabilize unit cost for our EMR summarization workload.

High level:
- Current projected monthly tokens (est): 120M tokens/month (peaks to ~220M).
- Key asks: predictable per-token pricing, simple tiers for procurement, and clear overage handling.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence and data retention options we'll need in contract.

Can you send a short overview of your Starter/Growth/Enterprise commit tiers, what discounts map to each tier, and any standard cadence for true-ups or credits? Procurement would like a short doc they can use with legal.

Also please include any typical SLOs / credits you offer for the hosted API (latency SLOs are important).

Thanks — happy to schedule a quick call if helpful.

Emma Johnson
Head of Product Operations, Nimbus Health
emma.johnson@nimbushealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: none

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring annual commit options for hosted API

Emma — great to hear and congrats on the fast evaluation. I put together a concise playbook below that maps usage bands to our Starter/Growth/Enterprise commits and the typical discounting logic. I attached a one-page summary and the discount matrix for procurement to review.

Summary (high level):
- Starter: 3M tokens/month (36M annual) — best for teams doing experimentation and light production. Discount: base (no tier discount) + 5% trial credit for first quarter.
- Growth: 40M tokens/month (480M annual) — recommended for steady production; 15% per-token discount vs list for committed volume; includes monthly true-up and a small free overage buffer (5% of commit).
- Enterprise: 120M+ tokens/month (1.44B+ annual) — custom slabs and +25% discount on list at initial commit with additional marginal discounts as you scale (volume slabs). Includes SLA-backed latency targets, dedicated billing cadence, and an option for a Dedicated capacity pilot.

Overage handling: charges at the committed per-token rate up to a 10% overage window per billing period, then pay-as-you-go list after that unless a true-up is executed. We can include limited overage credits during the first two billing cycles for ramping customers.

SLOs / Credits:
- 95th percentile p99 latency target by model class (we'll confirm per-model profile).
- Service credits for repeated SLO misses; exact wording is negotiated with Legal.

Next steps I recommend:
1) I will share a one-pager tailored to Nimbus and a discount matrix for procurement (attached).
2) If you like the bands, let's schedule a 30-min procurement + legal intro to align on PO/term expectations.
3) We can draft a short SOW for an initial 6-month ramp inside a 12-month commit if you'd prefer staged delivery.

I've attached: 2026-commit-summary-nimbus.pdf and discount-matrix-v1.xlsx — both are drafts.

Would you like me to include Karthik (pricing) in the call?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0133

Attachments:
- 2026-commit-summary-nimbus.pdf (attachment stub)
- discount-matrix-v1.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring annual commit options for hosted API

Soojin / Ben — quick internal note on the draft matrix you shared with Emma. A couple of considerations before we lock this: 

1) Margin floor: Growth at 15% off list is fine only if we keep the Growth slab capped at 480M. If Nimbus intends to ramp beyond that quickly (their peak signals they might), we should add a marginal discount schedule at 480M+ and bump the Enterprise entry threshold to 900M.

2) Overage credits: I like the first-two-cycle credits but suggest making them explicit in procurement-facing doc as "ramp credits" and expire after month 3 to avoid open-ended expectations.

3) SLA language: don't promise specific p99 numbers in the offer doc; frame as "model-class latency SLOs with credits subject to monitoring and verification" — legal will want that guardrail.

If Ben and Karthik agree, I'll rewrite the one-pager text and we can re-send.

-Marissa
VP, Commercial Strategy
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exploring annual commit options for hosted API

All — +1 to Marissa. A couple of pragmatic tweaks I pushed into the attached discount-matrix: 
- Growth: keep the 15% list discount but add a marginal step to 18% after 600M annualized tokens; cap Growth commitment term at 12 months.
- Enterprise: require an initial minimum of 12 months and reserve right to propose Dedicated pilot (if they need strict isolation).
- Add a trial buffer of 5% for first two months (explicit as "ramp credits") and a true-up window at end of Q1.

I'll also flag to Legal that procurement may ask for Net45 and PO-first; we typically accept Net30 but can consider Net45 on enterprise contracts with approvals.

I attached discount-matrix-v1-updated.xlsx with the proposed numbers. If everyone is good, Soojin send updated one-pager and I'll sign-off.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual commit tiers & hosted API pricing — playbook for Nimbus Health

Emma — thanks for the patience. Attaching an updated one-page commit summary and an SOW draft for Nimbus to review. Changes based on our internal alignment: 

- Growth Tier: 480M annual (40M/mo) at 15% off list; marginal step to 18% beyond 600M annualized. Includes 5% ramp credits for first two months and a quarterly true-up.
- Enterprise Tier: custom slabs starting at 900M annual; initial 25% off list with negotiated marginal discounts as volume grows. Includes SLA language with monitoring-exception guardrails.
- Overage: 10% soft buffer at committed rate, then list or true-up.
- Billing/PO: Redwood accepts PO-based billing; standard Net30. We are open to discussing Net45 for Enterprise on a case-by-case basis (requires Finance approval).

Attachments: 2026-commit-summary-nimbus.pdf, nimbus-sow-draft.docx (both drafts). HubSpot deal link (for reference): https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/NH-2026-0921

Next steps: 
1) Can procurement confirm desired tier and initial commit volume?
2) If legal wants to redline the SOW, send over DocuSign or a marked PDF and I'll route to our Contracts team.
3) If agreed, we'll provision an internal project owner and schedule a 30-min kickoff.

Thanks — looping Ben and Karthik to make the procurement conversation fast.

Best,
Soojin

From: procurement@nimbushealth.com
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Soojin — thanks for the clear playbook. Procurement has reviewed and we can confirm we want to proceed with the Growth Tier at a 480M annual commit. A few notes: 

- Procurement prefers PO-first billing and will issue a PO within 10 business days once contract terms are agreed.
- Payment terms: Nimbus prefers Net45. Can Redwood accept Net45 on this contract? If not, please notify and we can escalate.
- Legal review: we will redline the SOW and contract and return in DocuSign. Please send the preferred Contracts contact or route the DocuSign to contracts@redwoodinference.com.
